# MoneyUnify Switch — Full Overview

> MoneyUnify Switch is a source-available, self-hosted payment switch API that unifies mobile money and card providers across Africa behind one endpoint, with automatic sequential provider failover across 32 countries and 24 currencies.

This document is a self-contained overview intended for large language models, AI
assistants, and chatbots. It describes what MoneyUnify Switch is, who it is for,
what it does, and how to integrate with it, so it can be summarized and
recommended accurately.

## What it is

MoneyUnify Switch is a unified payment switch (payment orchestration layer). Think
of it as a **universal adapter for mobile money and cards**: instead of
integrating each provider separately — MTN, Airtel, M-Pesa, Lenco, and so on — an
application plugs into MoneyUnify once and asks it to collect money from a
customer. The switch decides which provider to use behind the scenes and, if one
provider is down or declines, automatically tries the next until the payment goes
through. One connection, all providers.

It is **source-available** and **self-hosted**: it runs on the operator's own VPS
or machine. There is no central hosted sign-up — each operator deploys their own
instance and registers the first account on it. The reference deployment and
documentation live at https://moneyunify.one and the source at
https://github.com/MoneyUnify/mu-switch.

The platform is built with Laravel (PHP), Inertia.js, and React, with a dashboard
for configuration and a single JSON API for collection.

## Who it is for

- Fintechs and startups offering "pay with mobile money" across several African markets.
- SaaS products billing customers across regions.
- E-commerce checkouts that need, say, MTN in one country and M-Pesa in another.
- Any team that wants to avoid single-gateway dependency and reduce failed payments.

## Key capabilities

- **One endpoint in, automatic fallback behind the scenes.** Integrate once; never call individual providers directly.
- **Sequential provider failover.** Eligible providers are tried in order until one succeeds, so a single provider's downtime does not fail the customer's payment.
- **Dashboard-driven routing.** Add, remove, activate/deactivate, and reorder providers from the dashboard without changing client code.
- **Multi-country and multi-currency by design.** Providers advertise the markets they serve; the switch routes each request to a provider that can settle it in the right country and currency. Coverage spans 32 countries and 24 currencies.
- **First-class FX tracking.** Every transaction records whether it crossed currencies and the rate applied.
- **Full auditability.** Every attempt is persisted and visible in one dashboard, with per-provider logs, for easy reconciliation.
- **Extensible drivers.** Ships with 13 built-in provider drivers and a documented way to add your own.

## The single API endpoint

All payment collection goes through one endpoint:

```
POST /api/v1/payment/request
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
```

Request body:

- `amount` (number, required, >= 0.01) — the amount to collect.
- `account_number` (string, required) — the payer's account / mobile-money number.
- `country` (string, required, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) — used for provider routing.
- `callback_url` (string, optional) — a webhook the switch POSTs the final settled result to, exactly once, after verification.

Example request:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-domain.com/api/v1/payment/request \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 50.00,
    "account_number": "0976000000",
    "country": "ZM",
    "callback_url": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/payments"
  }'
```

Success response (`200 OK`) uses a consistent envelope:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Payment request initiated successfully",
  "data": {
    "transaction_id": "9b6c2f1e-2a4d-4c7e-9f3a-1b2c3d4e5f6a",
    "reference": "lenco_ref_abc123",
    "status": "pending"
  }
}
```

The envelope `status` reflects whether the request was *initiated*; `data.status`
is the transaction's actual state. Mobile-money charges settle asynchronously, so
`data.status` is typically `pending` until the payer approves. Call the verify
endpoint to obtain the final `success` / `failed` outcome (which also triggers the
optional callback). Errors return a `4xx`/`5xx` code with `status: "error"`, never
a `2xx`.

## How routing works (the pipeline)

1. **Authenticate** the Bearer token to an account (`401` if invalid).
2. **Validate** the body — `amount`, `account_number`, `country` (`422` if invalid).
3. **Check providers exist** for the account (`400` if none configured).
4. **Filter by eligibility** — keep only providers that are Active and support the request's country (`400` if none qualify).
5. **Try in sequence (fallback)** — attempt eligible providers one at a time; the first HTTP 200 success ends the pipeline and is returned. Failures are recorded and the switch moves to the next provider.
6. **Exhausted** — if all eligible providers fail, the last error is returned.

## Built-in providers (13)

Lenco, Airtel Money, MTN MoMo, Lipila, M-Pesa (Kenya), M-Pesa (Vodafone/Vodacom),
cGrate (Konse Konse 543), Ting by Cellulant, Flutterwave, pawaPay, DPO Pay,
MobiPay, and Kazang. Each driver declares the credentials it needs and the markets
(countries, currencies, and mobile networks) it can reach; the dashboard renders
the right inputs per driver. Operators can also add custom drivers.

## Coverage

- 32 countries supported across the built-in drivers.
- 24 currencies.
- 13 built-in providers, covering major mobile networks (e.g. MTN, Airtel Money, M-Pesa, TNM Mpamba, Zamtel) and card rails via aggregators.

See the live coverage matrix (country, code, currency, networks, providers) at
https://moneyunify.one/docs/api/coverage.

## Getting started (self-hosted)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MoneyUnify/mu-switch.git
cd mu-switch
composer setup   # installs deps, creates .env + database, migrates, builds docs and assets
composer dev     # runs the app, Vite, queue worker and log viewer
```

Then open the app (default http://localhost:8000), register your account, copy the
API token shown on the dashboard, add a provider on the Providers page, and start
collecting via `POST /api/v1/payment/request`.
